questions.question: What is layering? Name any two types of layering.
questions.solution_html:
• Layering is a vegetative method of plant propagation where a stem or branch is encouraged to
  • develop roots while still attached to the parent plant. Once roots form, the new plant is detached
  • and grown independently. Layering is a highly successful, low-maintenance, and reliable
  • method of vegetative propagation that allows new plants to develop roots while still receiving
  • water, nutrients, and hormones from the parent plant. It is ideal for woody plants and ensures
  • high success rates by creating a large, mature, and genetically identical, new plant.
  • Two common types of layering are
  • ❖ Air Layering (Marcottage): A section of an aerial stem is wounded, wrapped with moist
  • moss/soil, and covered with plastic to induce rooting.
  • ❖ Simple Layering (Ground Layering): A low-growing branch is bent to the ground
  • partially buried, and anchored to form roots.
questions.final_answer: partially buried, and anchored to form roots
